audience: CIO, with IT operations, SRE, network operations, security, risk and procurement leads in the room
purpose: show a CIO a real, near-term opportunity in IT operations that is cheap to test, and what they would need to find out; presented by a McKinsey team, non-commercial (no fees, no pitch)
zeroops: ZeroOps is the aim of running routine incidents with no manual work: detected, triaged and resolved automatically, with people focused on the novel and the risky.
governing_thought: AI agents for incident response became a real category in 2026, yet the routine judgment calls (is it real, whose is it, how bad, act or page) still sit with rules and whoever is on call, across application incidents and network monitoring alike. A typed decision model like TypeSafe's Jev could make those calls in a fraction of a second, with probabilities that code the organisation owns turns into act, ask a person, or log. A working demo on synthetic incidents showed the mechanism end to end. Whether it holds on real tickets is cheap to find out in three short stages, each ending in a decision, and we would be glad to help.

opportunity_levers.name: Routing
opportunity_levers.hypothesis: Fewer reassignment hops; tickets reach the resolving team sooner, during incident surges too
opportunity_levers.needs: Reassignment is frequent and costly; assignment groups can be told apart from ticket text; the licensed platform doesn't already do it (Q1, Q8, Q9)
opportunity_levers.measure: Reassignment count and time to the resolving group, replayed on closed tickets and surge periods

opportunity_levers.name: Triage
opportunity_levers.hypothesis: Consistent severity, major-incident and paging calls in about {p50} ms, each logged
opportunity_levers.needs: Text at first triage says enough; past severity labels are good enough to score against (Q3, Q10)
opportunity_levers.measure: Agreement with postmortem severity; major-incident recall; pages avoided overnight and during surges

opportunity_levers.name: Reversible fixes
opportunity_levers.hypothesis: Rollback, restart and scale-up run automatically behind a gate in owned code; people take the novel and risky
opportunity_levers.needs: Fixes already scripted and trusted; thresholds set on held-out history; a named owner (Q5, Q6, Q23)
opportunity_levers.measure: Share automated at the agreed threshold; reversals; incidents that should have gone to a person

opportunity_levers.name: Economics
opportunity_levers.hypothesis: Inference is close to free (about {cents} cents per 1,000 incidents), so the value rests on accuracy on real tickets
opportunity_levers.needs: Accuracy beats current rules and simple alternatives by enough to matter (Q19)
opportunity_levers.measure: Replay accuracy against current rules; fully loaded first-year cost

key_patterns: cascade: your rules first -> Jev for the judgment call -> a person when the gate isn't sure
guardrail: act only if confidence is high AND the action is reversible; thresholds owned by named people and checked on held-out data
fallback: on timeout, missing answer or low confidence, fall through to today's rules (fail closed)
